articles.title: Wardogs Players Really Want You To Close The Doors … Or Else
articles.summary: The hottest game on PC right now is Wardogs, the Battlefield-like mass multiplayer FPS by developer Bulkhead that's soaring up the Steam charts. While it may not be as hot as the game itself, the game's subreddit is full of hotheads demanding you do one teeny-tiny thing. Close. The. Doors. Behind.
body: Released in a closed beta state in August 2026 before entering early access in September 2026, Wardogs has taken PC gaming by storm. It's not only the number-one trending game according to SteamDB, with an all-time peak of 428,666 concurrent players on September 13, but it's also the fourth-most-played game on Steam, trailing behind Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and PUBG: Battlegrounds. Folks can't get enough of being a dog of war.
Something folks would love to get enough of, though? Players leaving those gosh-darn doors and gates open when venturing out onto the battlefield.

All over the official Wardogs subreddit are a ton of players decrying the carelessness of other players when it comes to not closing doors and gates behind them. Redditor demonmit1 posted on September 14, pleading for people to stop building so many gates and close the ones they open.

"If you're helping build a FOB, please… We only need one air locked gate for logistics," demonmit1 said. "No one closes them anyways, so adding more is not good. Stop it. If someone wants to leave the base, they can jump over a wall. They don't need to leave through a door they'll forget to close."

articles.title: Star Trek: Will the Saga of the Resurrected Captain Kirk End in Triumph or Tragedy?
articles.summary: IDW's critically acclaimed Star Trek: The Last Starship has reached its endgame. We chat with writers Collin Kelly and Jackson Lanzing to find out more about how it caps off the story of the resurrected James T. Kirk.
body: The Star Trek franchise may be in a bit of a weird place right now following the cancellation of Star Trek: Starfleet Academy and the impending end of Strange New Worlds, but never let it be said that there aren't great stories being told in this iconic sci-fi universe. Look no further than IDW's Star Trek: The Last Starship, a book that explores the aftermath of the horrific event known as The Burn. This series has seen the resurrection of Captain James T. Kirk in the 31st century, but can even a man as heroic as Kirk guide the Federation through its darkest hour? Is that even his goal anymore?

Everything in the series is coming to a head now as writers Collin Kelly and Jackson Lanzing prepare to wrap up their dramatic saga with The Last Starship #12 in October. It all comes down to the two driving forces of the series - Kirk and Captain Delacourt Sato - as they seek to put aside their differences and forge an alliance to save the galaxy from ruin.

First, check out an exclusive preview of Star Trek: The Last Starship #11 (due out on September 16), and then read on to learn more about how Kelly and Lanzing aim to cap off the series with a bang to rival that of The Burn itself.

articles.title: Live-Action Crazy Taxi Movie, New Sonic Animated Series, and Stranger Than Heaven Adaptation Heading to Netflix
articles.summary: Netflix has announced three Sega video game adaptations: a live-action comedy Crazy Taxi movie, a new Sonic animated series, and an adaptation of RGG Studio's yet to be released Stranger Than Heaven.
body: The Crazy Taxi movie is described as ‘live-action comedy,' and the Stranger Than Heaven adaptation is 'live-action crime.’ The new Sonic animation is obviously for kids.

Crazy Taxi comes first. It’s written by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand, the duo behind the 2025 reboot of The Naked Gun. Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, and Toru Nakahara, the producers behind the Sonic franchise, are on board to produce.

“Great games already have what every adaptation is chasing — characters people love, worlds they know by heart, and fandoms that show up,” commented Brandon Riegg, VP of Nonfiction and Transmedia at Netflix. “With Crazy Taxi, Sonic, and Stranger Than Heaven, we get to work across three completely different eras of Sega’s catalog, celebrating everything fans love, while introducing them to new audiences.”

articles.title: Lies of P Trademark Appears to Spell Out Sequel's Name
articles.summary: Lies of P looks set to be followed by "Wonders of O," according to a new trademark listing. Developer Neowiz appears to have trademarked the title via the EU Intellectual Property Office, for use in an upcoming game (as spotted by PhraseMaker ).
body: But while "P" was a reference to Pinocchio, what could "O" stand for? Well, fans of the puppet-starring Soulslike already think they know the answer, following various teases pointing to The Wizard of Oz and its character Dorothy — including a cameo from the Kansas heroine during the game's post-credits scene.

Indeed, Lies of P fans have spent the last two years discussing their hopes for what a Wizard of Oz Soulslike might look like, with villains such as the flying monkeys, living trees and, of course, The Wicked Witch of the West. I'd like to see players take Toto down too.

"What if Dorothy needs to return to Oz to purge the corruption that Paracelsus has created?" wrote a fan in one of the various reddit threads discussing hopes for an Oz-based sequel, many of which date back a couple of years. "Paracelsus is clearly a deceiver — as was the Wizard of Oz, so they may be one and the same? Or he is continuing the work of the original Wizard of Oz and is the 'new' Wizard of Oz?"

articles.title: The Last Of Us 2 Multiplayer Mod Canceled “On Behalf Of Sony,” Dev Says
articles.summary: Naughty Dog's The Last of Us franchise featured a multiplayer mode in Factions, and while the studio planned to add multiplayer to the sequel, it abandoned those ambitions before release.
body: Modder @Speclizer_ said on social media that the mod was due to launch this month. However, they said they "recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released."

Speclizer said this is an "extremely sad" development, but they hope people who supported the project will stick with them for the next one. Their next project will be "something of my own" as opposed to an extension of an existing game.
"Thank you all for the incredible amount of support over the last year. I hope to bring you something bigger and better soon!" Speclizer said.

Naughty Dog was set to expand The Last of Us into an online multiplayer experience in a very big way with The Last of Us Online. The game was in development for years with significant resources dedicated to it, and it was reportedly almost ready for release. However, in December 2023, Naughty Dog canceled the game, saying at the time that it was going to focus on single-player games instead.

articles.title: Red Dead 2 Actor Shares A Gross Secret About The Game
articles.summary: Actor Roger Clark played Arthur Morgan in Rockstar's celebrated 2018 Western Red Dead Redemption 2, and his performance was memorable for many reasons. In the game, Arthur suffers from tuberculosis, and he coughs a lot as a result.
body: Clark told Cade Onder that he had "five years to spread it out," regarding his voice-capture performance in Red Dead 2, and that's part of the reason why it wasn't as difficult as you might imagine. Additionally, Clark said if he was performing a "really bad coughing scene," this would be saved for the end of a given recording day, when his voice was already hoarse from all the work.
Beyond this, Clark said over that five-year period, when he recorded his lines, he, like most people, got sick--and he used this to his benefit.

"In five years, there's plenty of colds. There was a lot of data we got that was pretty damn genuine. I'd be like 'Hey, I've got a cold, let me get in there.' And they'd be like, 'Okay.' Nice good bit of phlegm," he said.

In addition to his leading role in Red Dead 2, Clark is known for his roles in the games Fort Solis, Rosewater, and Marathon. He won Best Performance for his role as Arthur Morgan at The Game Awards in 2018.

articles.summary: After years of rumours, and 10 months since its official unveiling, Valve's long-awaited standalone VR headset, Steam Frame, is poised to begin shipping soon, and with a confirmed starting price of £889.
body: Frame marks Valve's first VR headset since 2019's Index, and it represents a significant upgrade in almost every regard - from better screens and substantially reduced weight to movement and position tracking that's now handled on-device rather than external base stations.

Its improvements are perhaps less dramatic compared to more modern consumer VR headsets like Meta Quest 3, but they're still notable and you can find full specs on Valve's website. I've been playing with Frame for around two weeks at this point, incidentally, and you'll find more detailed impressions of the device in my Steam Frame review.

articles.title: "It's absolutely our goal to expand the market" - Valve's new Steam Frame VR headset has a nifty idea for broader appeal
articles.summary: Valve has said its new Steam Frame VR headset, despite costing nearly £900 for a base model, is intended to "expand the market" of virtual reality headsets. That's both because it's lightweight and standalone, but also because it addresses a fundamental and long-running problem VR headsets have had.
body: "For a long time, VR has turned itself into an accessory for your PC," Valve software engineer Jeremy Selan told Eurogamer in an interview ahead of Steam Frame's pricing announcement, "or in the case even of standalone, something that you have to decide to do first. Like, you might say, 'I want to play a non-VR game on my TV or on my PC,' or, 'I want to go try this specific VR experience.'" Regardless, it's an either-or situation - one or the other.

"From the outset of this product, we were really looking to do something new and to try to make customers not have to think if they wanted to do VR or non-VR games," Selan said. Therefore, a much bigger emphasis has been put on your ability to easily switch between VR and non-VR games - or movies or web browsing - while using the device.

"The non-VR experience is something that I use all the time," Selan went on, "and it's so comfortable because of the ergonomics of the controllers, the lightweightness of the device where you can carry it and use it in a bunch of rooms. So I find myself with this device for the first time putting it on, not even having decided what I'm going to play.

body: Good Gamer Group is a publisher that helps organize NDA’d playtests for upcoming games. The company’s latest post is looking for “top-ranked 2D fighting game players” to take part in an in-person session in Culver City, Calif., from Sept. 14 to Sept. 15. Specifically, they are looking for those who "have achieved a rank in the top 25% of a major 2D fighting game." Although this description doesn’t sound like a lot to go on, many are speculating that the playtest is for an unannounced sequel to NetherRealm Studios’ Injustice series.

The fact that the playtest is for an “unreleased AAA 2D fighting game” disqualifies just about every announced but unreleased title in the genre: Virtua Fighter: Crossroads and Dead or Alive 7 are 3D fighters, while Melty Blood Type Twi-Lumina isn’t AAA.

articles.title: Sega and Netflix partner for a "cute yet cool" Sonic TV Show, a Crazy Taxi film, and a "badass action" Stranger Than Heaven adaptation
articles.summary: Netflix is binge-producing video game adaptations faster than a certain Blue Blur can chow down a chilli dog. The streamer has just announced a new partnership with Sega to make another animated TV show based on Sonic the Hedgehog, as well as films adapting Crazy Taxi and the upcoming Stranger Than…
body: The multi-project deal supposedly begins with a feature-film adaptation of Crazy Taxi, Sega's long-running series of whacky arcade racing games that's being revived soon, penned by the screenwriting duo responsible for last year's The Naked Gun reboot (Dan Gregor and Doug Mand). The producers behind the surprisingly good live-action Sonic films (Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, and Sega's Toru Nakahara) are also involved with this one, per Variety. No telling if it'll be animated or live-action, though.

On the flip side, the Sonic Netflix series is set to be an animated romp that, according to Sega, is "high-voltage, comedic, yet emotionally grounded" and is "built for kids who want to feel a little edge, a little attitude, and a lot of 'that's my crew' wish fulfillment." Expect to see lots of the extended anthropomorphic Sonic family, then. Nakahara and animation director Carlos Stevens are attached.

And, finally, we have a film adaptation of Stranger Than Heaven also planned. RGG Studio's crime-ridden action game isn't due to come out until next year, 15 January, but Sega's giving it the multimedia treatment early.

articles.title: Mahershala Ali’s New Movie From Blade Director Is Getting Perfect Reviews
articles.summary: For years, fans hoped to see Mahershala Ali on the big screen as Blade in the MCU. That dream has finally ended with the actor closing the door on the project for good earlier this year, but there is a silver lining.
body: Across 17 initial reviews, Rotten Tomatoes has Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother sitting at a perfect 100%. It's not just certified fresh, it's a certified masterpiece. The film follows Ali as a religiously devout hitman who fights his way across Houston to protect his children following the death of his wife. The action is especially impressive and reflects Ali's preparation for Blade. Ali is joined by a cast that includes John Cho, Giancarlo Esposito, and Tramell Tillman, among others.

Praise is universally given to Ali's performance and the overall aesthetic of the film. Zachary Lee at TheWrap wrote that "what Ali, Tariq and the collaborators have assembled feels not just like kismet but divinely ordained, as if this was the movie they were always meant to make." While Ali and Tariq's Blade will always remain a " what if? ", audiences will be happy that something as good as Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother came out of it.

body: Tags included in the IP notice include "interactive multimedia software for playing games; computer software for use in providing multiple user access to a global computer information network; computer game software downloadable from a global computer network and wireless devices; computer game software downloadable from a global computer network" and so on, so it's safe to say we are looking at the registration of a video game here. Additionally, Neowiz is the owner of the application. All signs point to this being a sequel.

In terms of the name, you don't need to be a detective to work out the naming pattern there, do you? I wonder what the 'O' could refer to. Oz, perhaps - from The Oz books that form a book series that begins with The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), by L. Frank Baum. There are 14 books in the Oz canon, so there will certainly be plenty to draw from there, if that's where the Korean developers choose to go with the sequel. Will it be connected to Lies of P at all, or just a standalone project? It remains to be seen. It's also worth noting that the post-credits scene of the first game seemed to feature Dorothy - heroine of the first few Oz books. Go figure.
